nodes.label: Cinema as Information Space
nodes.description: The interpretation of cinema as an interface to events taking place in 3D space, similar to how new media interfaces present dense information.

nodes.label: Aesthetics of Density
nodes.description: A visual style characterized by a high density of information or objects, evident in web portals, GUI interfaces, and multi-layered digital films.

nodes.label: Dutch Painting (17th Century)
nodes.description: A historical precursor to the aesthetics of density, focused on detailed description and cataloging objects rather than hierarchical narration.

nodes.label: Christian Boustani's Films
nodes.description: Computer films that develop the aesthetics of density through digital compositing, using hundreds of layers to achieve unprecedented information density in cinema.

nodes.label: Digital Compositing
nodes.description: A digital technique that enables the seamless combination of numerous layers and allows every detail to be in focus, overcoming the depth-of-field limits of analog cinema.

nodes.label: Spatial Montage
nodes.description: A technique presenting multiple audio-visual streams simultaneously, akin to modern computer multi-tasking, challenging traditional temporal montage.

nodes.label: Cinema as a Code
nodes.description: The realization that in the computer age, cinema and other cultural forms become digital code (data) used to communicate experiences.

nodes.label: ASCII Films (Vuk Cosic)
nodes.description: Artworks that perform the new status of media as digital data by visibly displaying the ASCII code alongside the film image.

nodes.label: Media Translation
nodes.description: The continuous process of translating media content between formats, often resurrected as obsolete media in net.art.

nodes.label: Cultural Open Source
nodes.description: The effect of computerization that opens up traditional cultural techniques for redefinition, such as database challenging narrative and spatial montage challenging temporal montage.
